title: Image buttons need alternative text
summary: An <input type="image"> button has no alt text, so a screen reader cannot say what it does. Add an alt attribute that names the action.
problem: An <input type="image"> element is a button drawn as a picture, often a magnifying glass for search or an arrow for submit. It has no alt attribute, no aria-label and no title, so assistive technology has no name to announce for it.
whoItAffects: People using a screen reader hear only "button" or the image file name, so they cannot tell a search button from a purchase button. Voice control users also have no name to say, such as "click Search", to activate it.
steps: Search your templates for input elements with type="image". The scan result shows the exact markup.
Add an alt attribute that names the action the button performs, such as alt="Search" or alt="Place order".
Describe the action, not the picture. Write alt="Search", not alt="Magnifying glass".
If you prefer, replace the element with a
before:
<form action="/search">
  <input type="text" name="q" aria-label="Search the shop">
  <input type="image" src="/images/search.png" width="24" height="24">
</form>
after:
<form action="/search">
  <input type="text" name="q" aria-label="Search the shop">
  <input type="image" src="/images/search.png" width="24" height="24" alt="Search">
</form>
whyItMatters: A button without a name blocks the very action it exists for. This fails WCAG 1.1.1 (non-text content) and 4.1.2 (name, role, value), both Level A, and a visitor who cannot find the search or checkout button cannot finish their task.
howToCheck: Open the browser accessibility inspector, select the image button and read its Name. It should be a short action such as "Search". An empty Name means the alt attribute is missing.
